newsitem.title: USA: Motorola Q1 semiconductors turn a profit.
newsitem.headline: Motorola Q1 semiconductors turn a profit.

text.p: Motorola Inc said on Monday that, while sales from its semiconductor products segment fell 16 percent from year ago levels and orders declined five percent, the segment returned to profitability from an operating loss in the 1996 fourth quarter.

While semiconductor sales and orders were lower than first quarter 1996 levels, orders improved from fourth quarter 1996, as the business emerged from last year's semiconductor industry recession, Motorola said in a statement.
Steps taken in several business segments last year to reduce costs are beginning to have a favorable impact, it said.
Orders for semiconductors rose in the Asia-Pacific region and Europe, but declined in the Americas and Japan. The automotive market segment posted the highest order growth.
In its Land Mobile Products Segment, Motorola said sales increased 18 percent to $977 million. Orders rose 36 percent and operating profits were higher.

Orders for iDEN, its Integrated Digital Enhanced Network equipment, were up significantly, including more than $200 million from Nextel Communications Inc in the U.S. In addition, orders were received for new iDEN systems in Brazil and South Korea, it said.

In its Cellular Products Segment, sales rose four percent to $2.7 billion. Orders rose three percent and operating profits were higher, it said. The segment includes results of the Cellular Subscriber Sector (CSS), the Cellular Infrastructure Group (CIG) and the Network Management Group.
CSS sales increased, led by Europe, the Pan America region, China and the Asia-Pacific region, while they declined in Japan and South Korea, Motorola said.
Sales and orders of Global System for Mobil Communications (GSM) phones were up significantly, as demand for an entirely new GSM product line has been very strong, it said.
Orders in total declined slightly, as higher orders in Europe, the Asia-Pacific region, the Pan America region and China were offset by lower orders in Japan and South Korea.

CIG sales declined in comparison with a very strong first quarter a year ago, when results benefited from replacement of a competitor's entire system in the Philippines. Higher sales in the Pan America region were offset by lower sales in the Asia-Pacific region, Japan, China and Europe.
Orders increased, led by Japan and the Asia-Pacific region, while they declined in China, Europe and the Pan America region.
